topic: Evidence from the Deccan Riots Commission
questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"A peasant cultivator named Vithoba from Poona district gave the following testimony before the Deccan Riots Commission in 1876: 'I borrowed Rs. 50 from the Marwari sahukar seven years ago during a drought. I have repaid him more than Rs. 150 in grain and cash over the years. Yet, whenever I ask for my bond back, he claims that the interest has accumulated to Rs. 300. He never gives me a receipt for the grain I deliver. Three years ago, he forced me to sign a blank piece of paper with a stamp on it, saying that under the new Limitation Law of 1859 the old bond had expired. He threatened that if I did not sign, he would obtain a decree from the civil court and auction my bullocks and ancestral land. We rioted at Supa not to kill the sahukars, but to seize and burn those cursed debt books (bahi-khatas) that had made us slaves.'"

How did moneylenders manipulate the Limitation Law of 1859 to escalate the debt burden on illiterate peasants?

options.text: They returned all mortgaged lands to the cultivators voluntarily
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: They lowered interest rates to zero to attract new borrowers
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: They petitioned the British Parliament to cancel all peasant debts
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: They forced ryots to sign new loan bonds every three years, rolling unpaid compound interest into the new principal debt
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Evidence from the Deccan Riots Commission.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Evidence from the Deccan Riots Commission (Colonialism and Rural Society (Colonialism and Countryside)):
1. The Limitation Law limited bonds to 3 years; moneylenders bypassed this by forcing ryots to sign new bonds compounding overdue interest into fresh debt.
Hence Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
